result.title: BodyBridge: Grounded Body Layers for Sim-to-Real Translation of Vulnerable Road Users
result.summary: Simulation-to-real driving video diffusion models can translate photorealistic scenes, but they typically represent pedestrians and cyclists, vulnerable road users (VRUs), as generic object classes. This is insufficient for vulnerable road users whose safety-relevant appearance depends on articulated pose and identity. We present BodyBridge and Grounded Body Layers (GBL), a simulator-derived, pixel-aligned representation that combines scene geometry, canonical per-pixel body correspondence, and exact VRU masks. GBL provides explicit articulation to the video diffusion model, emphasizes VRU regions during control-branch post-training, and supports additive composition with scene-geometry control at inference. It also enables per-joint evaluation of generated VRUs and a failure taxonomy for identity errors. On CARLA-to-real translation, BodyBridge improves near-range PCK@0.5 by 22% over the released depth-conditioned baseline. Replacing normal-map body control with canonical correspondence reduces body flips by 18%, while composition reduces near-range facing flips by 27%. These results show that explicit body grounding complements scene-level control and improves pose-faithful VRU generation. All code, data, and model checkpoints will be made publicly available to support reproducible, pedestrian-aware autonomous driving research.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BodyBridge 与 Grounded Body Layers（GBL），一种由仿真器导出的像素对齐表示，融合场景几何、逐像素规范人体对应关系与精确 VRU 掩码，作为视频扩散模型的显式姿态控制，用于 CARLA→真实的弱势道路使用者生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「像素对齐的规范对应 + 掩码加权控制分支后训练 + 推理期可加组合」可能为 LVR 中如何把实体几何与区域证据保留在内部状态、以及如何施加接地监督提供可核查线索，但属生成控制而非推理状态，需较多核查。
